headline: On 113 teenagers aged 12 to 17 it never saw, the ask model from college students, unchanged, scored an AUC of 0.85 for their next PHQ-2 (0.78 to 0.92). Asking the top 23% by its score landed on a high answer 74% of the time, against 41% for asking at random. Over all 635 later answers it scored 0.90.
caveats: Only 113 teens answered again, mostly German-speaking, during the pandemic. The interval is wide.
The answers are not weekly: the median gap was 4 days before the first follow-up. Teens chose when to answer, and the ones who came back may differ from the ones who did not.
There is no check-in in this survey, so this tests only the earlier-answers part of the model.
The PHQ-2 here uses the adolescent wording, which adds "irritable". It is a screening score, not a diagnosis.
